content:
Hi people, new to Palomar here.
I have an ongoing submission, with "No blocking problems" identified. But the AI revision found a toolchain version inconsistency at README (I was aided by an agent who was trying to use a release candidate version, and I later decided to go for a "stable" one, or at least, not an rc).

Is there any danger that by correcting this problem and resubmitting, the AI verification might ("nondeterministically"?) fail the second time?

Or, should I register it as is, and then post a new version?
Thanks in advance!

EDIT I decided to commit the correction to the README (after a more detailed reading of the review, it did suggest that) and resubmit. Now waiting for CI.

Update. In fact, correcting this minor error and running verification again did not result in offering registry. But after addressing the further AI comments, I was authorized to ask for registration.

Now waiting, I'll keep the thread open until there is some further feedback at the submission web page.

EDIT. It's finally online! So I guess that's it, unless someone wants to add any suggestion about the questions of the first post :pray:
